result.oneSentenceSummary: add_members adds duplicate members without dedup or transaction

def add_members
    group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)
    usernames = params.require(:usernames)

    return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic

    existing_ids = group.user_ids
    Group.transaction do
      usernames.split(",").each do |username|
        if user = User.find_by_username(username)
          next if existing_ids.include?(user.id)
          group.add(user)

result.improvedCode:
def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
        # A message was filtered upstream: there is no payload to decode and no
        # partition/offset attached to the FilteredPayload sentinel itself.
        if isinstance(message.value, FilteredPayload):
            return

        try:
            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
            partition = message.value.partition
            offset = message.value.offset

            if isinstance(message.payload, FilteredPayload):
                # Nothing to decode, but the message still needs its offset
                # recorded and completed so it can be committed.
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
                return

            result = self.decoder(message.payload)

            if result is None:
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
                return

            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)

            work_item = WorkItem(
                partition=partition,
                offset=offset,
                result=result,
                message=message,
            )

            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)

        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
                )
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
                )

judge.titleReason: The title correctly says filtered payloads are sent to the decoder, but it also claims their offsets are never tracked, which the reference says is wrong for BrokerValue-wrapped filtered messages.

    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
        """
        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
        """
        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues

    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
        """
        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
        """
        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]

        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
        # Bounded queue: blocks here when the worker falls behind, applying
        # backpressure to the producer instead of growing without limit.
        work_queue.put(work_item)

judge.titleReason: The title names the defect: the work queues are unbounded and apply no backpressure.
judge.fixReason: Setting maxsize=1000 makes put() block when a queue is full, which applies backpressure without dropping messages, keeps hashing and FIFO order unchanged, and still registers the offset before enqueueing; the only other change is a comment.

result.improvedCode:
def transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(
    query_columns: Sequence[str],
) -> list[str]:
    """
    Transform aggregation functions to use sum(sample_weight) instead of count()
    for error upsampling. Only called when all projects are allowlisted.
    """
    import re

    transformed_columns = []
    for column in query_columns:
        # Match any valid spelling of count() (case/whitespace variations) and
        # preserve an optional alias so downstream references keep working.
        match = re.match(
            r"^\s*count\s*\(\s*\)\s*(?:as\s+(\w+))?\s*$", column, re.IGNORECASE
        )
        if match:
            alias = match.group(1) or "count"
            # Any count() becomes sum of sample weights
            transformed_columns.append(f"upsampled_count() as {alias}")

        else:
            transformed_columns.append(column)

    return transformed_columns

judge.titleReason: The title correctly says that `count()` matching misses aliased and whitespace-variant forms, which is the defect described.
judge.fixReason: The case-insensitive full-string regex accepts whitespace inside the parentheses and around the expression, keeps an explicit alias with its original case (defaulting to `count`), and leaves all other columns unchanged and in order.
